newsitem.title: JAPAN: Too early to say sales tax hike will hurt - BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Too early to say sales tax hike will hurt - BOJ.

text.p: It is too early to say whether a scheduled increase in Japan's sales tax next April will reduce consumption substantially in the fiscal year starting on April 1, Masayuki Matsushima, director of the BOJ's research and statistics department, said on Wednesday.
He said a planned increase in the consumption tax to five percent from three percent would inevitably have some sort of impact on consumption, but it was uncertain yet how great that impact would be.
Corporate investment and consumption decisions have been made for some time with the planned rise in mind, he said.
"It is too early conclude that the tax rise will substantially reduce consumption in 1997/98," he said.
